profile.summary: Uni-RNA is a pre-trained language model for RNA sequences from DP Technology. It reads an RNA sequence and returns a learned representation (embedding) for each position, or predicted probabilities for masked positions. The authors fine-tune these representations for RNA structure and function prediction tasks.
profile.summary_source_locator: bioRxiv abstract; README.md: Model summary and Quick Start

summary_quotes.text: we developed a novel context-aware deep learning model named Uni-RNA that performs pre-training on the largest dataset of RNA sequences
through fine-tuning, our model achieved the state-of-the-art (SOTA) performances in a spectrum of downstream tasks, including both structural and functional predictions
outputs the MLM head logits for each position

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Uni-RNA is a Transformer encoder with a masked-language-model head: the masked-LM class outputs, for each position, logits over the token vocabulary. The released configurations use 64-dimensional attention heads, a GELU feed-forward layer three times the hidden size, rotary position embeddings and a vocabulary of 10 tokens; in the L16 upload these are four special tokens (<pad>, <eos>, <cls>, <mask>) and the letters N, A, T, C, G and U. The last hidden layer gives per-position embeddings that can be used directly or fine-tuned for a downstream task. The training data and pre-training details are described in the preprint, whose full text was not read here.
sections.source_locator: README.md: Model summary, Quick Start; bioRxiv abstract

quotes.text: Default configs use 64-d attention heads, GELU feed-forward with width `3 * hidden_size`, rotary position embeddings, vocab size 10.
`UniRNAForMaskedLM` (a MaskedLM-style class): outputs the MLM head logits for each position (shape `[batch, seq_len+2, vocab_size]`), representing token prediction probabilities

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Three checkpoints are released: L8 (8 layers, hidden size 512), L12 (12 layers, hidden size 768) and L16 (16 layers, hidden size 1024). The repository distributes them together as one weights archive on Google Drive, with no version label. Uploads named UniRNA-L8, UniRNA-L12 and UniRNA-L16 also exist on Hugging Face under the EscheWang account, but the repository README does not link to them. A result should name the checkpoint (L8, L12 or L16) and where the weights came from.

facts.value: Pre-trained RNA language model with a masked-language-model head

quotes.text: named Uni-RNA that performs pre-training on the largest dataset of RNA sequences

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer encoder with rotary position embeddings, 64-dimensional attention heads and a GELU feed-forward layer of width 3 times the hidden size. L8: 8 layers, hidden 512, 8 heads. L12: 12 layers, hidden 768, 12 heads. L16: 16 layers, hidden 1024, 16 heads.

quotes.text: Default configs use 64-d attention heads, GELU feed-forward with width `3 * hidden_size`, rotary position embeddings, vocab size 10.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: RNA sequence as a string of upper-case letters, or FASTA files for batch embedding. Lower-case letters are mapped to the unknown token.
facts.source_locator: README.md: Quick Start; Ultra fast embedding inference

quotes.text: You must convert string to uppercase before inputting the sequence to the model
all the lowercase letters will be merged and converted to `unk_token` in the tokenizer
Prepare a fasta file, same format as the `example/fasta/example_0.fasta` file.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Per-position embeddings from the last hidden layer, optional attention weights, or masked-LM logits of shape [batch, sequence length + 2, vocabulary size].

quotes.text: outputs the MLM head logits for each position (shape `[batch, seq_len+2, vocab_size]`)
if you want return attention weights, set output_attentions=True

run_guide.summary: Install the Uni-RNA code, unpack the released weights and write embeddings for the example FASTA files with the L16 checkpoint.
prerequisites: Conda and Python 3.10, as the README's install commands use.
A CUDA-capable GPU: the README installs PyTorch from the cu126 wheel index, and the embedding script assigns one thread per GPU. Memory needs are not stated.
The weights archive (weights.tar.gz), downloaded by hand from the Google Drive link in the README.
The code is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0: non-commercial use only. No licence is stated for the weights.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/ComDec/unirna_tf.git
cd unirna_tf
git checkout --detach d4f26510af1034ef132b9b45df4737cfb6092f61
steps.explanation: Clone the repository and pin it to the commit read for this page. The clone and checkout lines are added; the README asks for a git repository because the package reads git information for its version.

quotes.text: We need git info. to track the version of the code.

steps.title: Install
steps.shell:
conda create -n unirna python=3.10
pip3 install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install -e .
steps.explanation: The README's install commands. Activate the unirna environment after creating it; the README does not show that line.

quotes.text: conda create -n unirna python=3.10 pip3 install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126 pip install -r requirements.txt pip install -e .

steps.title: Unpack the weights
steps.explanation: First download weights.tar.gz by hand from the Google Drive link in the README and copy it to the repository root. The archive unpacks to a weights directory holding the checkpoints, for example weights/unirna_L16.

quotes.text: For model weights, please download from [Google Drive]
copy to the root directory of the project, then run: `tar -zxvf weights.tar.gz`. You will find the model weights is stored in the `weights` directory.

steps.title: Embed the example sequences
steps.explanation: Runs the README's embedding command on the example FASTA files with the L16 checkpoint on one GPU. Raise --concurrency to the number of GPUs and --batch_size to what GPU memory allows. The README also shows a Python Quick Start; its no_grad block uses torch without importing it.

quotes.text: The `--batch_size` is the batch size for each thread, depending on the GPU RAM size of your machine.

outputs: An embedding for each sequence in the FASTA files, written under example/output. The README does not describe the file format.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The weights download is manual and the archive is not versioned.

notes: The repository ComDec/unirna_tf calls itself the official implementation; its owner account is named Xi Wang, the same name as the preprint's first author (checked through the GitHub API, not a saved source). The Hugging Face uploads EscheWang/UniRNA-L8, -L12 and -L16 are not linked from the README, have no model card and no licence field; their parameter counts and the L16 context value are used with that caveat. MultiMolecule hosts an unofficial port, not used. bioRxiv full text returned HTTP 429 twice.
